response_schema.description: Standard response format for all pipeline stages. Every stage MUST return output in this format. All fields are REQUIRED to ensure predictable, parseable JSON output.

fields.field: Unique identifier for the stage. Must match stage filename.
Overall execution result. Values: success | partial | failed.
Execution trace. Captures timing, reasoning, validation.
ISO8601 timestamp when stage began.
ISO8601 timestamp when stage finished.
Execution time in milliseconds.
List of thinking-framework steps executed.
Key choices made during execution with reasoning.
Assumptions made due to missing or ambiguous input.
Non-critical issues that did not block execution.
Critical issues encountered.
Gate check results: passed (bool) + checks array.
Array of all sources accessed during stage execution. Provides traceability for all data.
Full URL of the source.
Title or description of the source.
How source was accessed: search | fetch | api | cache.
List of what information was taken from this source.
Structured reasoning trace showing how conclusions were reached. Maps to 9-step workflow.
Step 1: How the input was interpreted and understood.
Step 2: Key patterns, insights, and analysis performed.
Step 3: Approach chosen and reasoning behind the choice.
Step 4: Action sequence created with checkpoints.
Step 5: What was done and key decisions made during execution.
Step 6: Validation results, issues found, and edge cases checked.
Step 7: Improvements made without expanding scope.
Step 8: Handoff preparation and format verification.
Step 9: How findings were combined into coherent output.
Array of key decisions made with alternatives and rationale.
High-level summary of stage results for quick review.
The ONE most important discovery or result.
3-5 critical takeaways from the stage.
Overall confidence: high | medium | low.
Explanation of confidence level.
Stage-specific deliverable data. Schema defined per stage.
Actionable guidance for the subsequent stage.
What the next stage should focus on first.
Potential issues or risks to monitor.
Any caveats or limitations about provided data.
Readiness indicator. Signals pass to next stage.
Boolean indicating if output is complete for next stage.
Identifier of the stage that should receive this output.
List of items required by next stage but not provided.
Optional catch-all object for any additional data not covered by standard fields. Use descriptive keys. Keeps schema predictable while allowing flexibility.
